# 0068: Imports stay in the top import section and Ruff checks the whole repository

Status: accepted, 2026-10-12.
Extends [0039](0039-the-package-listing-is-the-architecture.md) with an import-placement rule alongside the layer-boundary rules.

## Context

Function-local imports hide dependency links from a reader scanning the top of a file.
They also defer import failures until a particular path executes.
The price curator had seven such imports, despite already importing the package at startup.
The existing lint command checked only source and tests, leaving repository scripts outside the gate.

## Decision

**Runtime imports belong in the top import section.** Imports inside functions and classes are forbidden.
Ruff's `PLC0415` checks that rule, and the existing `E402` rejects module imports placed after executable statements.
No suppressions are added for either rule.

**Type-only imports remain in the top import section's `TYPE_CHECKING` block.** Ruff permits this existing pattern.
These declarations expose annotation dependencies without introducing runtime cycles across the layers (ADR 0039).

**`make check` runs Ruff over the whole repository.** Tracked Python scripts receive the same rules as source and tests.
Generated caches and third-party directories remain outside discovery through Ruff's standard exclusions and Git ignore rules.
The command uses the project's locked Ruff, whose minimum version is `0.12.0`, where `PLC0415` became available.

## Consequences

The curator's dependencies are visible before its functions.
Future function-local imports fail CI, including those added to repository scripts.
A runtime dependency cycle must be resolved structurally rather than hidden behind a deferred import.
Type-only dependencies remain visible without changing when their modules execute.

## Lens

Hidden imports hide dependency links.
Keep dependencies visible at the top of each file, and make violations fail the same check contributors and CI run.
